items.label: f03-result-bridge-forgery
items.front: A DOM/React ticket runs learner code in the same iframe document as the bridge script, and the host accepts any {kind:'result', id} message from that frame. Evidence: src/runner/client.ts:92-93.
items.back: Learner code can post its own 'all passed' result for the run, so progress is not tamper-resistant. Accepted as a non-goal; the store's known-test-name check only limits forgeries to real test names.

items.label: f02-review-note-anchor-unchecked
items.front: An author adds a ticket whose review note points at a file that does not exist and line 400 of a 3-line solution. Evidence: validate-content only checks hint text, note count, the 40-word limit and concepts (scripts/validate-content.ts:8-14).
items.back: The build passes and learners see a review note anchored to nothing. Verify review[].file and review[].line by hand, or extend the validator to resolve them against solutionFiles.

items.label: f01-runtime-cache-stale
items.front: You rebuild the sandbox runtime bundle (sandbox-worker.js) while the app tab stays open, then run a ticket. Evidence: runtimeCache is a module-level object filled on first fetch and never cleared (src/runner/client.ts:2-11).
items.back: The run still uses the old bundle text for the whole page lifetime, so the rebuild looks like it had no effect. Reload the page, or key/invalidate the cache by build version.

items.prompt: A ticket has testNames A and B. A run reports two passing results, both named A. Why does suitePassed return false even though the result count equals the number of known tests?

choices.text: It also needs distinct result names to cover every test, and {A} has size 1
It returns true: count equality and every result passing are the only conditions
It compares names case-insensitively and rejects any repeated name as forged
Duplicate result names make result.error non-empty, which fails the first check

choices: It also needs distinct result names to cover every test, and {A} has size 1
It returns true: count equality and every result passing are the only conditions
It compares names case-insensitively and rejects any repeated name as forged
Duplicate result names make result.error non-empty, which fails the first check

items.explanation: The last clause new Set(result.results.map(t => t.name)).size === known.size stops a forged or buggy result list from repeating one name: {A} has size 1, not 2.

items.prompt: A learner's last passing day was Monday, they skip Tuesday and pass on Wednesday (first ever skip). Weeks later they skip one day again. What does updateStreak do on that second skip?

choices.text: It continues, because the grace day is restored after seven passing days in a row
It is set to 0, and the learner must pass twice the next day to restart it
It resets to 1, because the one lifetime grace day was used and is never refilled
It continues, because a gap of exactly two days is always bridged by the streak

choices: It continues, because the grace day is restored after seven passing days in a row
It is set to 0, and the learner must pass twice the next day to restart it
It resets to 1, because the one lifetime grace day was used and is never refilled
It continues, because a gap of exactly two days is always bridged by the streak

items.explanation: gap === 2 only bridges when !freezeUsed, and freezeUsed becomes true the first time gap === 2; nothing in updateStreak sets it back to false.

items.prompt: Two learner submissions hang: one contains `while (true) {}`, the other awaits `new Promise(() => {})`. Why do they end with different timeout messages?

choices.text: The loop hits the 30 s compile timeout, as loops are detected while transpiling the code
The guard rejects the promise after 2.5 s, while the loop blocks until the 10 s start-up timeout
The loop trips the 2.5 s in-sandbox guard, while the promise waits for the host's 3 s deadline
Both hit the host's 3 s deadline, and the worker and iframe runtimes word it differently

choices: The loop hits the 30 s compile timeout, as loops are detected while transpiling the code
The guard rejects the promise after 2.5 s, while the loop blocks until the 10 s start-up timeout
The loop trips the 2.5 s in-sandbox guard, while the promise waits for the host's 3 s deadline
Both hit the host's 3 s deadline, and the worker and iframe runtimes word it differently

items.explanation: harness.ts sets deadline = start + 2500 and guard() throws when instrumented code (such as the loop body) runs past it; a never-settling promise runs no guarded code. client.ts arms a separate 3000 ms timer after the frame's ready message.

items.prompt: A learner passes a ticket, then reruns the same passing code twice more. Why does their XP for that ticket not grow?

choices.text: Each rerun earns XP, but a daily cap clamps the total back to the ticket's xp
XP is recomputed from the deduplicated passed test names, which reruns don't grow
The UI blocks repeat runs after the first pass, so recordRun is never called
recordRun skips the XP calculation once the ticket is already marked passed

choices: Each rerun earns XP, but a daily cap clamps the total back to the ticket's xp
XP is recomputed from the deduplicated passed test names, which reruns don't grow
The UI blocks repeat runs after the first pass, so recordRun is never called
recordRun skips the XP calculation once the ticket is already marked passed

items.explanation: names = [...new Set([...old names, ...newly passed names])] and earned = testXP(ticket, names.length, hints); the earned value only changes when a new test name appears, so the delta is zero.

items.prompt: During an active recall session the learner opens one hint, then passes the suite after the due date. What is the effect on the recall schedule and on their hint count?

choices.text: The recall advances, but its next interval is reset to 1 day as help was used
It is flagged assisted and cannot advance, and hintsUsed stays the same
hintsUsed rises by one and costs XP, and the due recall still advances as usual
Nothing is recorded, as hints are disabled while a recall session is active

choices: The recall advances, but its next interval is reset to 1 day as help was used
It is flagged assisted and cannot advance, and hintsUsed stays the same
hintsUsed rises by one and costs XP, and the due recall still advances as usual
Nothing is recorded, as hints are disabled while a recall session is active

items.explanation: useHint returns early for an active recall, setting recall.assisted = true without touching progress.hintsUsed; recordRun's spaced check requires !recall.assisted.

items.prompt: hintMultiplier always returns 1, so hints never reduce XP. What reasoning does the app give for removing the old hint penalty?

choices.text: A penalty rewards avoiding help when stuck, and unassisted recall measures mastery
Hints were used too rarely for the penalty to change any learner's XP total
Hint usage is not recorded at all, so there is nothing left to penalize
Penalties made XP totals impossible to recompute when restoring old backups

choices: A penalty rewards avoiding help when stuck, and unassisted recall measures mastery
Hints were used too rarely for the penalty to change any learner's XP total
Hint usage is not recorded at all, so there is nothing left to penalize
Penalties made XP totals impossible to recompute when restoring old backups

items.explanation: README: asking for help is compatible with learning; independent mastery is measured later by unassisted recall instead. Hints are still recorded (hintsUsed).

items.prompt: An author writes one hidden test as `test("Handles empty input", ...)` with double quotes. `seed()` builds `testNames` with the regex `/test\('([^']+)'/g`. What happens when `npm run validate-content` runs the reference?

choices.text: The harness refuses to register the test, so the reference passes with one test fewer
The test runs and is counted, as the regex also matches double-quoted names
The compiler worker rejects the test file as a syntax error before any test runs
The test runs but is missing from testNames, so the count mismatches and it FAILs

choices: The harness refuses to register the test, so the reference passes with one test fewer
The test runs and is counted, as the regex also matches double-quoted names
The compiler worker rejects the test file as a syntax error before any test runs
The test runs but is missing from testNames, so the count mismatches and it FAILs

items.explanation: The regex only captures single-quoted names; validate-content compares result.results.length with ticket.testNames.length and reports the ticket as FAIL on the mismatch.

items.prompt: Pure-JS tickets run in a blob Web Worker, yet the host does not create that worker itself; it ships bridge code that creates it inside the sandbox iframe. What would be lost if the host page created the worker directly?

choices.text: The worker would inherit the host's permissive policy, not the iframe's strict CSP
The worker could no longer import the learner's sibling modules from the bundle
The worker would gain DOM access, as page-created workers share its document
Nothing security-relevant; the iframe only exists so the 3 s deadline can end it

choices: The worker would inherit the host's permissive policy, not the iframe's strict CSP
The worker could no longer import the learner's sibling modules from the bundle
The worker would gain DOM access, as page-created workers share its document
Nothing security-relevant; the iframe only exists so the 3 s deadline can end it

items.explanation: client.ts comments that a blob worker inherits the opaque-origin frame's CSP; DECISIONS says worker runtimes are created inside the restricted iframe for that reason.

items.prompt: A hand-edited backup sets `earned` for a ticket to 9999 and lists one real test name in passedTests. What does the import do with that XP?

choices.text: It caps earned at the ticket's xp value but otherwise trusts the stored number
It keeps 9999, as earned values are trusted once the backup passes the size limit
It ignores 9999 and recomputes earned from the validated passed test names
It rejects the whole backup, as an earned value above the ticket's xp is invalid

choices: It caps earned at the ticket's xp value but otherwise trusts the stored number
It keeps 9999, as earned values are trusted once the backup passes the size limit
It ignores 9999 and recomputes earned from the validated passed test names
It rejects the whole backup, as an earned value above the ticket's xp is invalid

items.explanation: Imports throw on unknown test names, dedupe the rest, then set result.earned[t.id] = testXP(t, names.length, hints): totals are recalculated from known test names, never taken from the stored figure.

items.prompt: A learner starts a recall session one day before it is due and passes it without hints. Why does the recall schedule not advance?

choices.text: The pass is discarded, as recall sessions cannot run tests before they are due
Early sessions are treated as assisted, which also removes the existing recall count
Only a session started at or after the due time counts as spaced and advances it
The schedule does advance, but the next interval is shortened for the early start

choices: The pass is discarded, as recall sessions cannot run tests before they are due
Early sessions are treated as assisted, which also removes the existing recall count
Only a session started at or after the due time counts as spaced and advances it
The schedule does advance, but the next interval is shortened for the early start

items.explanation: spaced requires Date.parse(recall.startedAt) >= due, plus passed, not previously passed and not assisted; recalls only increments when spaced is true. Early practice passes but leaves the recall count unchanged.

items.prompt: The worker runtime already replaces fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and friends with throwing stubs. Why does the sandbox iframe still need `connect-src 'none'` and the rest of its CSP?

choices.text: Stubbing globals blocks just the APIs you thought of, and other request paths remain
Without the CSP the stubs could be deleted, since defineProperty left them configurable
The CSP is there only to stop learner code reading the host page's localStorage
The stubs are installed after learner code runs, so the CSP covers the gap before

choices: Stubbing globals blocks just the APIs you thought of, and other request paths remain
Without the CSP the stubs could be deleted, since defineProperty left them configurable
The CSP is there only to stop learner code reading the host page's localStorage
The stubs are installed after learner code runs, so the CSP covers the gap before

items.explanation: DECISIONS: remote dynamic imports, resource elements, and alternative network APIs cannot bypass a browser-enforced policy the way they could bypass a simple fetch replacement. The stubs are defined writable:false, configurable:false.
